name: XRAI Glass
oneLine: A live captioning and translation app for phones that can also show the captions on compatible AR smart glasses, including XRAI's own AR2 glasses.

platforms.text: iPhone, iPad, Android, Windows; AR glasses
platforms.detail: XRAI offers free apps for iOS, Android and Windows, and the App Store version also runs on Apple silicon Macs and Apple Vision. Captions show on the phone or on compatible AR glasses; the pricing page lists the Windows and Mac desktop app under Ultimate.

deviceRequirements.detail: The App Store lists iOS 17.5 or later (or macOS 14.5 on a Mac with M1 or later), and XRAI's setup guide says Android 11 or newer. Glasses are optional; the AR2 glasses pair with a phone within about 10 m.

roomCaptions.detail: The app captions conversations around you through the phone's microphone, a Bluetooth microphone or the glasses' own microphones, and shows them on the phone or in AR glasses.

groupConversations.detail: XRAI suggests putting the phone in the middle of the table, or using a Bluetooth or conference microphone (it lists a 360° mic for 8+ people). XRAI Stream shares live captions to other devices on the same WiFi.

languages.detail: XRAI's pricing table counts languages and dialects: 20 on the free plan, 300 on Premium and Ultimate. Its app store listings say translation covers 140+ languages and dialects.

offline.text: Yes, on the free plan (less accurate)
offline.detail: The free Essentials plan includes unlimited offline captioning with engines on the phone. XRAI's help centre says this is much less accurate than its cloud engines and can sometimes invent words; the cloud engines need internet.

speakerLabels.detail: Speaker identification needs a paid plan and cloud transcription, and not every cloud engine supports it. People can be named by saying "Hey XRAI, my name is" and their name.

translation.text: Yes, live; two-way on paid plans
translation.detail: Premium and Ultimate translate live, with Auto-reverse for a two-language conversation and up to 10 spoken languages at once. For the free plan XRAI's pages disagree: the pricing page lists translation between 20 languages, a March 2026 help article says translation is not included.

saveTranscripts.detail: When you stop, you choose Keep or Discard; kept conversations are stored on the phone and can be searched. The pricing table lists unlimited history on Ultimate.

export.detail: XRAI's help centre describes emailing, texting or copying a saved conversation, and the store listings mention sharing audio recordings. Which plan includes export is unclear: the pricing table ticks Premium and Ultimate, the Ultimate card lists it as an Ultimate extra.

fileUpload.detail: Transcribing an uploaded audio or video file is not described on XRAI's pages.

summaries.text: Paid AI assistant; may need OpenAI key
summaries.detail: XRAI's app page lists an AI Assistant that summarises conversations and answers questions, as a paid (Pro) feature. An April 2025 help article says it needs a separate OpenAI account, charged per use.

customWords.detail: No way to add your own words or names is described on XRAI's pages.

display.detail: Font size and distance, colours, fonts, spacing, bionic reading and dark or light themes can be changed, and on glasses captions can be pinned and moved. A simpler Basic Mode is also available.

soundAlerts.detail: Alerts for sounds other than speech are not described.

phoneCalls.detail: Captioning phone calls is not described on XRAI's current pages.

videoCalls.text: Teams on Windows; page says Coming soon
videoCalls.detail: A May 2025 help article explains adding XRAI inside a Microsoft Teams meeting on a Windows PC, but XRAI's Teams page still says Coming soon. Zoom and Google Meet are not mentioned.

mediaOnDevice.detail: XRAI's TV page for shows and movies says Coming soon. Captioning audio playing on the phone is not described.

humanCaptioners.detail: No human captioners are described; captions are automatic.

privacy.detail: XRAI's privacy policy (July 2023) says free-plan audio is processed on the phone and deleted after the session unless you turn on audio recording, while paid-plan audio goes to third-party cloud providers. It doesn't say whether audio is used to train AI.

account.detail: Setup starts with an XRAI account or an Apple, Google, Microsoft or LinkedIn sign-in, then a code sent to your phone number.

availability.detail: XRAI states no country limits for the app. The AR2 glasses ship to the US, UK, Australia, Canada, Japan, Singapore, South Korea, New Zealand, the UAE, Taiwan, Hong Kong, China and Mexico.

freePlan.detail: Free Essentials includes unlimited offline captioning, up to 30 minutes per conversation and 1 day of history, without speaker identification. XRAI's pages disagree on whether it includes translation and smart glasses.

price.detail: XRAI's pricing page, October 2026: Premium US$20 a month or US$15 a month billed yearly, Ultimate US$40 or US$30 billed yearly; the US App Store lists Premium at US$19.99 a month or US$179.99 a year. The XRAI AR2 glasses cost US$699 with 3,600 pro minutes included.

accessibilityFunding.detail: XRAI says UK Access to Work can pay for its glasses, subscription and Bluetooth mics for employees, and the Disabled Students' Allowance covers XRAI AR One glasses for eligible students.

strengths.text: The phone app works without glasses, and the free plan includes unlimited offline captioning.
Captions can show on compatible AR glasses, including XRAI's own AR2 with 8+ hours of battery, right in front of your eyes.
Group and event tools: Bluetooth and conference microphones, and XRAI Stream to share live captions to other devices on one WiFi network.
Paid plans add speaker identification by name, two-way auto-reverse translation and up to 10 spoken languages at once.

limits.text: The free plan caps each conversation at 30 minutes and keeps history for 1 day.
XRAI says free offline transcription is much less accurate than its cloud engines and can invent words that were never spoken.
Premium includes 600 pro (cloud) captioning minutes a month, and the cloud engines need an internet connection.
Speaker identification needs a paid plan and a cloud engine that supports it.

notes: The XRAI pricing page (re-read 2026-10-28) contradicts itself: the Premium card says 'Unlimited conversation length' but the table says 60 minutes; the Ultimate card says 'Unlimited online captioning' but the table says 'Unlimited + 1,800 pro'; the Premium card lists 'Works with smart glasses' as an upgrade while the table ticks it for free Essentials too; the Ultimate card lists export as an Ultimate extra while the table ticks it for Premium too; the FAQ says unused pro minutes carry over while the table ticks rollover only for one plan; the free card says 'Translation between 20 languages' while the table gives Essentials no translation minutes and the help centre (31 Mar 2026) says translation is not included in Essentials. Only what the pages agree on is in a cell's text; the rest is in detail. Language counts differ: pricing table 20/300 languages and dialects, store listings 140+ for translation. Accuracy claims differ (98% offline in quiet one-to-one talk in the FAQ, >75% in the table, 'dramatically less accurate' in the help centre), so no accuracy figure is used. Website prices show '$' with no country; read as USD (they match the US App Store: $19.99 monthly, $179.99 annual). The App Store also lists 'XRAI Premium (6 Months) $179.99' and top-up packs. AR2 is $699 on the AR2 page but £699 on the glasses comparison page. A free trial is only mentioned in the privacy policy, with no length. Glasses have a 14-day return policy; subscriptions are non-refundable unless the law requires otherwise (s28). The AI assistant guide (April 2025) says users need their own OpenAI account; the app page marks AI Assistant as Pro, so it is unclear whether a key is still needed. Microsoft Teams: the platform page says 'Coming soon!' but a May 2025 help article explains how to use it. Device requirements: an older help article says iPhone/iPad 13.7 or later, the App Store says iOS 17.5 or later (store used). Company: App Store seller 'XRAI INC (NY)', Google Play developer 'Xrai Inc' (New York address), website footer 'XRAI Inc. Registered in the State of Delaware, USA', privacy policy names 'XRAI Limited' (England and Wales); the About page says the team is fully remote. The privacy policy dates from 22 July 2023 and does not mention AI training. A second, older Google Play listing exists (glass.xrai.captions); xrai.glass download links point to glass.xrai.us.subtitles. Phone-call captions appear only in 2022 press coverage, which was not used. Google Play pages were read by downloading the page HTML.
